doPostProcessing.description: If set to true then the passages are going to be post-processed using the #postProcessingFunction.

postProcessingFunction.description:
This is the function that is going to be applied when #doPostProcessing is set to true. The function would be modifying the {@link Genai.SourcePassage} using the args provided.
Here is an example of a Lambda function definition in Python:
```py
def replace_occurrence(sourcePassage, args):
    import re
    content = sourcePassage.contentStr
    mapping = args['replacementMapping']
    modified_content = content

    for acronym, expansion in mapping.items():
        modified_content = re.sub(fr'\b{acronym}\b', f"{acronym} (i.e. {expansion})", modified_content, flags=re.IGNORECASE)

    return sourcePassage.withContentStr(modified_content)

lambda_post_processing = c3.Lambda.fromPyFunc(replace_occurrence, actionRequirement='py')
```
In the previous example function, the user needs to provide `replacementMapping` in the args defined in #postProcessingArgs because it gets accessed within the function.
The Lambda needs to have a runtime associated that has all of the packages that are used within the function.

postProcessingArgs.description:
These are the function arguments to be passed to the #postProcessingFunction.
e.g. `{'replacementMapping': {'IMF': 'International Monetary Fund'}}`
